column1: # German (de) catalog. Same format as zh-hant.tsv:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
# (empty context = a plain UI string; `@id` = a command id; `@plural` = "one|other" forms).
# Clean-room: written from the meaning of VectorCraft's English labels in standard German, using the
# feature names German-speaking users of vector illustration software know (Zeichenfläche, Farbfelder,
# Kontur, Fläche, Pfad, Ankerpunkt, Zeichenstift, Direktauswahl, Pathfinder, Muster, Vorgabe, Ebene,
# Verlauf, Deckkraft, Schnittmaske, Verzerrungshülle). No other application's German localisation
# resource, string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add entries the same way.
# Conventions: commands use the infinitive (Öffnen, Speichern, Einblenden) and sentences address the
# user as "Sie"; nouns are capitalised as German requires, the rest of a label is not title-cased.
# Tools are "<Name>-Werkzeug", dialogs "Dialogfeld „…“", panels "Bedienfeld „…“". Quotation marks are
# „ “, the dash is –, prose uses the decimal comma and a space before % ("100 %"). Key names stay as
# the menus show shortcuts (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Esc), so a hint and its shortcut read alike. Status and
# error messages keep the case of their English first word, as they are often shown after "…: ".
# Coverage: the whole interface — every menu string and every `tl!` literal (`complete_menus`,
# tested) — and the status and error messages. Left in English on purpose (`MENU_KEEP_AS_IS` in the
# tests): the product name, language names, OpenType, the built-in workspace names and the bracketed
# perspective grid preset names; `de-DE`, `de-AT`, `de-CH` and every other `de-*` locale resolve here.
# Photoshop-style raster effects (Effect menu, their dialogs).
# Status and error messages too (`@msg` rows at the end, `COMPLETE_MESSAGES` in the tests).
# A native speaker's review is welcome: keep the placeholders ({name}), the trailing "…" and the
# leading/trailing spaces of fragments exactly as they are.
